title: You Can See Everything Passes $100 Million Worldwide in Rare Documentary Breakout
body_md:
You Can See Everything has crossed a milestone rarely achieved by theatrical documentaries, reaching $102.4 million at the worldwide box office. The film has earned $93.4 million domestically and another $9 million internationally, a striking result for a documentary running close to three hours and centered on the Elizabeth Holmes and Theranos scandal.

Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the project was produced quietly by A24 for approximately $7 million. It made a surprise world premiere at the Telluride Film Festival before developing strong word of mouth and critical momentum. Its domestic opening in mid-October brought in $15 million, and the film has remained a significant theatrical attraction through the fall rather than relying on a single opening-weekend burst.

The documentary follows events over three years, beginning as Holmes, the founder of health technology company Theranos, prepares to serve an 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors. Its success suggests that audiences have been willing to spend considerable time with a nonfiction examination of a corporate scandal, rather than treating the subject as material best suited to streaming alone.

The United Kingdom has become a notable new market. The film opened there with $3.2 million from 596 locations, giving A24 its second-largest opening in the territory after Backrooms, which debuted to $5.7 million. Approximately 70 percent of the British audience was younger than 35, mirroring a similarly youthful demographic pattern reported in the United States. Australia and New Zealand currently lead overseas markets with $3.8 million.

The international rollout is still unfolding. Screenings have begun in Turkey, Poland, the Czech Republic, Russia, the United Arab Emirates and Greece, while further releases are planned in Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Germany, Austria, Hong Kong, Spain, France and Japan. A24 is distributing in selected territories, with Sony handling other markets including parts of the Middle East and Scandinavia.

The milestone is impressive, but the documentary box-office record remains some distance away. Michael Moore's Fahrenheit 9/11 stands at approximately $222 million worldwide, while March of the Penguins reached $127 million. You Can See Everything has therefore established itself as a major nonfiction theatrical hit without yet becoming the highest-grossing documentary of all time.

Its continued international expansion will determine how far the total can climb. For now, the most striking elements of the run are its relatively modest production cost, sustained word of mouth and unusually strong appeal among younger moviegoers.
excerpt:
The Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim documentary has reached $102.4 million globally.
Its unusually strong theatrical run continues as international markets open.
